subject: Transition financing term sheet and performance comparison
messages:
From: Paul Harris <paul.harris@brightlane.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@brightlane.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transition financing term sheet and performance comparison

Hi Stephanie —

Great talking earlier. Brightlane is evaluating a move off our current inference vendor; our engineering team flagged a ~20% monthly cost gap and a few reliability incidents during peak batch jobs. Before we start a formal RFP, I wanted to ask if Redwood can provide: a concise term sheet that includes short-term onboarding credits and a performance comparison against our current provider (we mainly care about P95 latency at 2k tokens and steady-state throughput for 8 concurrent workers).

Attached is a one-page summary of our existing contract and usage patterns (current_contract_summary.xlsx). Key constraints: 1) a 90-day migration window, 2) we require SOC2 evidence and an audit trail for the pilot, and 3) we prefer a commercial structure that amortizes onboarding credits instead of a single upfront rebate.

Would you be able to share a draft term sheet and a quick perf benchmark matrix by Thursday? We are trying to keep this vendor change tight — pilot in Aug, decision early Sep.

Thanks,
Paul
Paul Harris
Head of Infrastructure Engineering, Brightlane Health
paul.harris@brightlane.com
[Attachment: current_contract_summary.xlsx (XLSX, 28KB)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Harris <paul.harris@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transition financing term sheet and performance comparison

Paul —

Thanks for the details and for sending the usage file. I put together an initial term sheet and a high-level performance note that maps to the metrics you called out. See attached: RDW-term-sheet-v1.pdf. High level of what we propose:

- Pilot credits: $25k in onboarding credits applied over first 90 days (amortized across invoices).
- Commitment tiers: three-month pilot (no long-term lock), with optional 12-month committed rate post-pilot that yields an additional 12% off list at the medium tier.
- Performance baseline: we can commit to P95 latency targets aligned to your 2k-token profile on our Dedicated cluster; we recommend a short perf run to validate for your specific prompts.

Two asks on our side:
1) Can your legal team share the primary SLAs in your current contract so we can align fallbacks?
2) For the perf run, can your SRE team provide a 2-hour window next week with a sample workload?

Cc'ing Marcus and Sean to align on pricing carveouts and the perf plan. If this looks directionally OK, I'll update and share a DocuSign-ready version.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
[Attachment: RDW-term-sheet-v1.pdf (PDF, 46KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transition financing term sheet and performance comparison

Thanks for the ping — reading RDW-term-sheet-v1. A couple of internal notes/suggestions before we send an external v2: 

- Offer structure: replace a one-time $25k credit with a ramped credit schedule (10k month 1, 8k month 2, 7k month 3). This reduces churn risk and aligns incentives.
- Billing carveouts: include an explicit egress cap for the pilot so they aren't surprised by data transfer charges.
- Risk allowance: propose a 30% contingency budget for ops engineering during cutover (we can call it "migration support credit") — flag this in the term sheet as an optional add-on.
- Performance validation: recommend we run a short A/B of their critical prompt set against our Dedicated config and their incumbent. Results should include cost per 1M tokens and p95 latency at target concurrency.

If the customer is price-sensitive, we can also propose a blended running rate: 6-month lookback to determine commit tier and then apply the committed discount retroactively on the pilot months if they convert. Keeps us flexible.

I'll drop a sample pricing spreadsheet in the thread.

Marcus
Director, Customer Economics
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transition financing term sheet and performance comparison

Attaching a quick models export (pricing-models.csv) with three scenarios run on Brightlane's reported usage:

Scenario A (Conservative): Pilot credits ramped as Marcus suggested. Effective unit cost beats incumbent by ~8% after credits, but initial month is cost-neutral. P95 target met on Dedicated with small KV cache tuning.

Scenario B (Convert-first): Larger upfront credit but aggressive committed rates (12-month). Beats incumbent by ~22% year-one, but requires a 12-month commit at medium tier.

Scenario C (Burst + Seat): Minimal commit, provide burst credits + seat-based premium for scaling concurrency. Better for their org if they want low lock-in; about ~10% better economics after 4 months.

Quick operational note: their current vendor had 2 incidents in the last 6 months tied to warm-start scale. We should highlight Redwood's graceful fallback options and our region routing to reduce immediate risk.

I'll mark up RDW-term-sheet-v1 with the specific numbers and hand back a v2 for Stephanie to send.

Sean
Sr. Solutions Engineer
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
[Attachment: pricing-models.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Harris <paul.harris@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, legal@brightlane.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transition financing term sheet and performance comparison

Paul —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the usage file and for the call earlier this week. We've incorporated internal feedback and attached a revised term sheet: RDW-term-sheet-v2.pdf. Key changes from the version you saw: 

- Ramp credits: $10k / $8k / $7k across the 90-day pilot (applies as invoice credits).
- Optional migration support credit line (up to $15k) to cover engineering handoff risk; opt-in line item.
- Pilot guardrails: egress cap during pilot and a defined perf validation window; we'll run an A/B with your 2k-token prompts and publish P95 + tokens-per-second + cost-per-1M-tokens.
- Commercial path: if Brightlane converts within 60 days of pilot, we'll apply an 8–12% committed discount depending on selected tier; otherwise, standard on-demand rates apply.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, sign the attached term sheet and we will schedule the perf run (2-hour window). DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/rdw/DOC-7821
2) Share the specific 2-hour window for the perf run and the SRE contact for the engineering test.
3) Legal: happy to take a short call to align the egress cap language and pilot acceptance definition.

HubSpot reference: HS-55012. I'll open a PO-friendly version if your procurement needs it.

Appreciate the partnership — we'll aim to make the migration low-friction.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
[Attachment: RDW-term-sheet-v2.pdf (PDF, 49KB)]
